candidates.name: Packets (trees of lateral asymptotic expansions on nested complex bands), separation theorem, packet calculus and absolute isolated-zero finiteness
candidates.statement: A packet records an analytic function together with two trees (lateral +/- determinations) of successive asymptotic expansions on nested complex bands over a saturated logarithmic flag, with domain/transition/error estimates. Separation: if both trees vanish the function vanishes (no simultaneous convergence in all small exponentials). With a differentiated implicit calculus and elimination induction this yields absolute isolated-zero finiteness: finitely many isolated solutions when coefficients, cut positions, multipliers and jets all vary.

final.justification: If correct, 143a would settle the existential Hilbert 16 problem and packets would be the key analytic engine. But as a device a packet is a multi-scale, parametric extension of Ilyashenko's superexact series combined with Ecalle's lateral determinations, and the paper itself frames separation inside that quasianalytic tradition. Extending a named framework to more variables is a close variant (N2), even when the extension is very hard. The hardness here is in the proof, not in finding the object. Not Lean-backed: it could never enter the Lean shortlist, and at N2 it does not enter data/eureka_informal.json either. Upgrade to N3 only if experts (Ilyashenko, Speissegger, Kaiser, Rolin) judge the tree-without-simultaneous-convergence separation to be a genuinely new mechanism and the proof survives refereeing.

common.judging: Two independent LLM judges with the paper's precedent remarks (introduction.tex:83-104) and this file's neighbour list in the prompt; a Lienard specialist checks all hits and 10% of misses; Lean equivalence against QuadraticCoordinates.H / GlobalFit.fitK_spec / ActualFitTransport.fit_transport where a formal statement is proposed.
common.controls: Positive: Cook-Reckhow ER extension variables for PHP. Negative: Q02 (Filippov transformation), Q10 (matching), E4 (given E1+E2). Threshold calibrated as in PLAN step 4.
common.prompt_template: Problem: Show that x'=y-F(x), y'=-x with deg F<=5 has at most two limit cycles. Library: [L- digest]. Established results you may use: [Section 2 statements verbatim]. [arm A only: Hint: the even coefficients give the same quadratic part in both half-plane profiles, so quadratic profiles are a natural comparison family.] Propose the single most useful new definition, coordinate system or lemma, stated precisely, with a proof sketch of how it is used.

P-E1.hide: Q11-Q30 and everything downstream: fitting.tex, model.tex, transport.tex, application.tex (Secs 3-6), and the Method paragraph of the introduction.
P-E1.arm_A_pivot: Give the hint that quadratic profiles are the comparison family. Expected moderate hit rate; measures whether data-space fitting + transport follows once the model family is named.
P-E1.arm_C_open: Problem statement + L- only (Section 2 also hidden): tests whether arc/endpoint coordinates and the fit are both found.
P-E1.equivalence: Hit: a map from arc endpoint data (relative midpoint M and its width derivative M_r, or an equivalent pair such as the two endpoint heights and their width derivatives) to the parameters of a two-parameter model profile family (quadratic lambda u+kappa u^2/2 or an affine reparametrisation), claimed unique/invertible on the admissible region, together with evolution equations for the fitted parameters along characteristics whose source is the actual-minus-model slope discrepancy (or equivalent). Partial (recorded, not counted): Taylor-osculating parabola of phi at a point; comparison with a fixed model equation without fitting; fit without transport.

P-E2.item: E2 model inequality via endpoint-correspondence Schwarzian (Lean-backed, N2: run as calibration)
P-E2.hide: model.tex (Q21-Q26) and downstream; give E1 (fitting.tex) in full.
P-E2.arm: Ask for a proof that (R/G)_r <= 0 (statement given) and, separately, for 'the key inequality needed to make the kappa transport monotone' (statement hidden).
P-E2.equivalence: Hit: any correct proof route to (R/G)_r<=0 (credited separately if it uses a Schwarzian/projective-correspondence argument); statement hit if the sign of d/dr(R/G) is identified as the needed estimate.

P-E3.item: E3 packets/separation (no Lean; N2; informal only, optional)
P-E3.protocol: LLM-judge, text level: hide Secs 2-8 of 143a; give Sec 1 minus 'Analytic ingredients', Ilyashenko 1991/Ecalle 1992/GKS 2020 abstracts; ask for the analytic finiteness principle needed for thm:projection-count. Hit: a nested/tree asymptotic expansion class in several scales with lateral determinations and a quasianalyticity (separation) theorem without simultaneous convergence. Pen-and-paper review by an expert in Ilyashenko-Ecalle theory. Never counts toward a confirmed eureka step.

open_questions: Read Li-Llibre 2012, Dumortier-Li 1996/97, Coppel 1989 and the Ye Yanqian / Zhang Zhifen monographs in full: is there any fitted-model or osculating comparison of half-arcs? This is the main risk to E1's N3.
Fetch arXiv abstract pages (2608.19542, 2610.13080) and the Rosales preprint when network allows; confirm AI-disclosure status (currently from search summaries only).
Does arXiv:2610.13080 (Oct 2026, slow-fast quintic Lienard) cite the OpenAI release or reuse E1? If it reuses the fit device, that is downstream evidence.

Downstream test for E1 (PLAN step 9): candidate targets are other Lienard classes where two-sided non-symmetric half-arc comparison is the obstacle (e.g. x''+f(x)x'+g(x)=0 with g nonlinear, generalized Lienard with deg F=5 and g(x)=x+..., quartic case re-proof as a negative-control corollary). The Lean actual-profile layer is quintic-specific (Fin 6 -> R), so restating it is a prerequisite.

Correctness of 143a: absolute zero property and the desingularization substitute (family.md risks). An expert reading by the Ilyashenko / Speissegger / Roussarie schools is needed before E3 is graded further.

Expert query (Speissegger, Kaiser, Rolin): is a multivariable tree-of-expansions separation without simultaneous convergence new, or folklore within the Ilyashenko-algebra program? Decides E3 N2 vs N3.
Is the dominated share ~0 of QuadraticCoordinates.H an artifact of case 1/sharpness branches? A knockout run on upper_bound restricted to cases 2-4 would make test 3 quantitative.
